cases.evidence: seg tags clustered with gaps <3 words (format error)
cases.cause: too-dense candidate tagging inside short noun phrases
cases.proposed_rule: Enforce a minimum token gap (e.g. ≥3 words) between candidate boundaries and avoid placing boundaries inside short NPs or quoted names; prefer after the NP head or sentence-final punctuation.

example_pair.input: It was ruled by the "Vichy" French. These were French people who had made peace with the Germans in 1940 and worked with the invaders instead of fighting them.
example_pair.output: It was ruled by the "Vichy" French. <SEG:1> These were French people who had made peace with the Germans in 1940 and worked with the invaders instead of fighting them.

cases.evidence: emitted subject/modality before clause head and negation, causing dropped 'not be surprised' or wrong subject assignment
cases.proposed_rule: Do not finalize a clause's subject or modality before the clause's main verb or negation is available; place candidate boundaries after the clause head (verb/negation) or its complement.

example_pair.input: All things considered, we should not be surprised if our own ancestors solved their "protein problem" in somewhat the same way that chimps on the savanna do today.
example_pair.output: All things considered, <SEG:1> we should not be surprised if our own ancestors solved their "protein problem" in somewhat the same way that chimps on the savanna do today.

cases.evidence: domain-specific noun ('wicket') was disambiguated incorrectly when emitted early (rendered as unrelated sense)
cases.cause: ambiguous domain-specific noun before disambiguating context (e.g. numeric/object words)
cases.proposed_rule: Delay committing translation for ambiguous domain-specific nouns until disambiguating collocates (numbers, objects, or domain markers like 'runs'/'wickets') are available; avoid boundaries that separate those collocates.

example_pair.input: But, after losing the captain's wicket India only made 36 runs loosing 7 wickets to end the innings.
example_pair.output: But, after losing the captain's wicket India only made 36 runs loosing 7 wickets to end the innings. <SEG:1>

cases.evidence: modifier ('national') was translated before its head, producing 'national team' instead of 'national park'
cases.cause: modifier committed before head noun arrived
cases.proposed_rule: Do not finalize translations of modifiers (adjectives/nominal modifiers) before the head noun arrives; prefer boundaries after the head noun.

example_pair.input: The Plitvice Lakes national park is heavily forested, mainly with beech, spruce, and fir trees, and features a mixture of Alpine and Mediterranean vegetation.
example_pair.output: The Plitvice Lakes national park <SEG:1> is heavily forested, mainly with beech, spruce, and fir trees, and features a mixture of Alpine and Mediterranean vegetation.

cases.evidence: segment ended after copula+predicative, separating it from its complement ('of the seven wonders...'), producing fragmented translations
cases.cause: copula/predicative split before its complement or relative clause
cases.proposed_rule: Avoid placing a boundary immediately after a copula + predicative expression when a complement (prepositional phrase or relative clause) follows; keep predicate+complement together.

example_pair.input: The Great Pyramid at Giza is the only one of the seven wonders that is still standing today.
example_pair.output: The Great Pyramid at Giza is the only one of the seven wonders that is still standing today. <SEG:1>

cases.evidence: numeric count got detached and contradicted the earlier clause when emitted separately
cases.cause: numeric quantifier separated from its clause/unit (split around punctuation like semicolon)
cases.proposed_rule: Keep numeric counts and their measures/units with the clause or phrase that introduces them; do not emit a boundary immediately before a numeric count that completes a preceding statement.

example_pair.input: However, the percentage of XDR-TB in the entire group of people with tuberculosis still seems to be low; 6,000 of the total 330,000 people infected at any particular moment in South Africa.
example_pair.output: However, the percentage of XDR-TB in the entire group of people with tuberculosis still seems to be low; <SEG:1> 6,000 of the total 330,000 people infected at any particular moment in South Africa.

cases.evidence: verb + preposition sequence was split, producing 'reflect a' separated from 'on a trip' and yielding ungrammatical output
cases.cause: splitting verb + particle/preposition from its object
cases.proposed_rule: Do not place boundaries between a verb (especially verbs that take prepositional particles) and its preposition/object; keep verb+particle+object contiguous.

example_pair.input: Sharing a field trip virtually is also a great way to reflect a on a trip and share experiences with future classes.
example_pair.output: Sharing a field trip virtually is also a great way to reflect on a trip and share experiences with future classes. <SEG:1>

summary: The prompt frequently places candidate boundaries that split linguistic heads from dependents: modifiers before their noun heads, subjects/modality before the main verb or negation, verbs from their prepositional particle/object, and numeric measures separated from their clause. It also clusters tags too densely inside short NPs (format errors). De-prioritise boundaries at positions that would cut modifier-head, predicate-complement, verb‑particle, or numeric-unit spans (the audit shows over-trust near relative positions 0/3 and 2/3).
